summary: The Gemara discusses the weight of the crimson thread used with the red heifer and the Yom Kippur goat, resolves a dispute about whether a non-priest may slaughter the red heifer, digresses on the customs of the people of Jericho, and concludes with the ish iti's impurity from carrying the Azazel goat.

display.whats: How much did the crimson thread weigh, and when does the ish iti become impure?
display.hint: Two disputes run in parallel: the weight of the crimson thread (for parah vs. Yom Kippur goat) and whether a non-priest may slaughter the parah. R. Yochanan boldly contradicts his own teacher on the latter.
display.title: Crimson Thread Weights and the Non-Priest Slaughter Dispute

learning.ahaMoment: R. Yochanan publicly contradicts his own teacher because he is convinced that non-priest slaughter is always valid - one of the few cases where a student overrules his teacher on record.
learning.memoryAnchor: Crimson thread: 10 zuz for the red cow, 2 sela for the Yom Kippur goat - and R. Yochanan tells a tanna to 'go teach that outside' when the tanna claims otherwise.
learning.learnerQuestion: How much did the crimson thread weigh for each rite, and may a non-priest validly slaughter the red heifer?
learning.coreTension: A baraita's crimson-thread weights for the red heifer and the Yom Kippur goat sit alongside a live dispute over whether the parah may be slaughtered by a non-priest, with R. Yochanan breaking from his own teacher's ruling that such slaughter is invalid.
learning.coreMove: R. Yochanan rejects the baraita's claim and the position of his own teacher R. Shimon ben Yehotzadak, ruling that non-priest slaughter of the parah has never been found invalid, while the digression on Jericho's customs and the ish iti's impurity round out the daf's practical details.

takeaway.text: The crimson thread weighed ten zuz for the red heifer and two sela for the Yom Kippur goat; R. Yochanan rules that non-priest slaughter of the parah is valid, even overruling his own teacher on the matter.

learning.learningBlocker: Learners may conflate the non-priest slaughter dispute (about the parah) with the Yom Kippur goat rite, since both share the crimson-thread theme on this daf, when the slaughter debate is specifically about parah.

misconceptions.misconception: The dispute over whether a non-priest may slaughter applies to the Yom Kippur goat sacrifice, since both are discussed together with the crimson thread.
misconceptions.correction: The non-priest slaughter dispute is specifically about the parah adumah (red heifer); the Yom Kippur goat is a separate rite, linked on this daf only by the shared crimson-thread theme.

quizSeeds.answer: Because the tanna claimed non-priest parah slaughter is invalid, and R. Yochanan held we have never found non-priest slaughter to be invalid.
quizSeeds.question: Why did R. Yochanan tell the tanna to 'go teach outside'?

sugyot.finalRuling: The ish iti becomes impure by carrying the goat; he must immerse and wait until nightfall.

glossary.en: The designated man who escorts and sends the Azazel goat to the wilderness cliff on Yom Kippur.
Red heifer - a cow whose ashes purify those contaminated by a corpse.
One who has immersed in a mikveh but not yet waited until nightfall for full purification.

rashiTranslations.en: Rashi: opens - [of the heifer, the weight is] ten denarii - [because it] requires weight; [of the] goat, [the weight is] two selas and that suffices.
Rashi: continues - [of the] leper - [the weight] is insufficient [from either of the above, so] just a shekel suffices.
Rashi: continues - this is our text: [the Amoraim] dispute regarding it - R. Shimon ben Halfta and the Rabbis dispute [regarding the specifications of the red] heifer.
Rashi: continues - and [there is] a sign [to remember the distinctions] - lest you err to say that one [Tanna] was saying [a weight of] two selas.
Rashi: continues - this Mishna [serves] as a sign for you: [as taught in] Tractate Menachot (folio 110:).
Rashi: continues - 'one who adds [more than the measure] and one who diminishes [less than the measure]'.
Rashi: continues - but provided [that] he intends his heart [toward] Heaven - [in this sign].
Rashi: continues - you will remember [how] to say that the one [Tanna] gave in it [the thread] a measure of the one who adds [more] than all of them.
Rashi: continues - and the one [Tanna] gave in it a measure of the one who diminishes [less] than all of them.
Rashi: continues - but a medium measure was not mentioned here [in the teaching].
Rashi: continues - [the Amoraim] do not dispute regarding the heifer.
Rashi: continues - [they dispute only] in the language [terminology] of the heifer - and that day.
Rashi: continues - [which day was] that? [When R. Nachum ben Kisi] spoke [and said]:
Rashi: continues - he atones - [meaning] the death of the righteous atones.
Rashi: continues - as [is] stated in general [in] Tractate Moed Katan (folio 28:).
Rashi: continues - why was the death of Aaron adjoined to the [High] Priest's garments?
Rashi: continues - [this is] to say to you: just as the [High] Priest's garments atone,
Rashi: continues - so [too] the death of the righteous atones.
Rashi: opens - of his heifer [referring to] the heifer of the High Priest on Yom Kippur.
Rashi: continues - [and the Mishna mentions] Elazar and its statute - [that] Elazar [is mentioned] in [Scripture].
Rashi: continues - and it is written [Numbers 19] 'and you shall give her to Elazar the Priest' etc.
Rashi: continues - and it is written [ibid.] 'this is the statute of the Torah' and everywhere that [the term] 'statute' is written,
Rashi: continues - it is a [binding] condition [that must be fulfilled].
Rashi: continues - [regarding] Aaron and [its] statute - [that the term] 'statute' is written [in Leviticus 16]: 'and Aaron shall bring [his chatat bull]'
Rashi: continues - the bull of the sin offering that is his, and he shall atone, etc., and he shall slaughter
Rashi: continues - the bull of the sin offering that is his, etc. And it is written
Rashi: continues - in Acharei Mot on the same matter (ibid.): 'and this shall be
Rashi: continues - for you an eternal statute, to atone for the children of Israel.'
Rashi: continues - slaughter is not a service: and the statute does not
Rashi: continues - apply to slaughter. Different is the heifer, for it is of the sanctity of
Rashi: continues - Temple upkeep (bedek habayit); that is, it does not have the sanctity of
Rashi: continues - the altar, but rather monetary sanctity alone.
Rashi: continues - for behold its slaughter is on the Mount of Anointing; therefore
Rashi: continues - there is no aspect of divided services in it, and all
Rashi: continues - the services are equal in it. And is this not a fortiori
Rashi: continues - as a rhetorical question. Regarding the slaughter of his [Aaron's] bull, which is of the sanctity of
Rashi: continues - the body, no statute is written for it; but regarding the slaughter of
Rashi: continues - the heifer a statute is written, and it is disqualified by a non-priest.
Rashi: continues - regarding the appearances of plagues, as it is written (Leviticus 13):
Rashi: continues - '(like a plague it appears),' and he shall be brought to Aaron
Rashi: continues - the priest.' 'And he shall slaughter it before him' - from the fact that it is written
Rashi: continues - 'before him,' implying that the slaughtering does not pertain to Elazar
Rashi: continues - directly, but rather 'and another shall slaughter it before
Rashi: continues - Elazar.' And Rav says: actually, Elazar himself slaughtered it,
Rashi: continues - and what does 'before him' mean? That he should not divert his attention from guarding it.
Rashi: continues - that only now does the heifer become fit. For behold
Rashi: continues - her whole being is made only for her ash.
Rashi: continues - 'to exclude what?' That a diversion of
Rashi: continues - attention does not disqualify in the performance of the heifer ritual. 'The gathering of her ash' - 'and a pure man shall gather,' etc.
Rashi: continues - (Numbers 19). 'And the filling of water' - to put into the ash for sprinkling. 'For sanctification' -
Rashi: continues - it is the placing of water on the ash and mixing them together.
Rashi: concludes - 'for keeping' - the daf ends mid-comment with this word from Numbers 19:9; the comment continues on 42b.
